solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Spatter liquid as worker in pub (7)

indicatorNotes.liquid: Liquid things flow and lose their shape, so the letters run into a new order.

annotation.surface: A careless drinker slops beer over the barman.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Liquid' looks like the thing being spattered, but it is the instruction to rearrange SPATTER.
annotation.definitionFit: A tapster is one who draws beer from the tap in an inn or pub.

entries.clue: Bird in rush, changing direction at last (4)

indicatorNotes.changing direction at last: The last letter is a direction, R for right, and it swaps to the other direction, L for left.

annotation.surface: A bird darts into a clump of rushes and veers off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rush' suggests the reed a bird would hide in; here it is the verb, TEAR.
annotation.definitionFit: The teal is a small freshwater duck.

entries.clue: Empty talk from chum, mean not disclosing age? (7)

indicatorNotes.not disclosing: Not disclosing the age means leaving AGE out of the word.

annotation.surface: A friend who is cagey about their age and does a lot of talking.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mean' is the noun, an average; take AGE out and AVER is left.
annotation.definitionFit: Palaver is lengthy, idle chatter.

entries.clue: What can dry up closed water source abruptly (5)

indicatorNotes.abruptly: Cut off abruptly: the word stops before its last letter.

blocks.note: a door pulled to is closed

annotation.surface: A spring that was capped suddenly runs dry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dry up' reads as a water source failing, but it means wiping the dishes. TO for closed comes from 'push the door to'.
annotation.definitionFit: A towel is used to dry up washed crockery.

entries.clue: Fanatical state’s dispatch ceding power to bishop (8)

indicatorNotes.ceding power to bishop: P for power gives way to B for bishop.

annotation.surface: A zealous regime sends out a decree handing authority to the church.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dispatch' pretends to be a state sending something; it is the noun meaning speed.
annotation.definitionFit: Rabidity is the condition of being rabid, fanatically extreme.

entries.clue: Woman is arch, beginning to tease (7)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: The beginning of 'tease' is its first letter.

annotation.surface: A woman described as arch and playfully teasing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Arch' reads as the adjective, mischievous, which suits a tease; it is the noun, a bridge.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain first-name definition: 'woman' stands for any woman's name, and Bridget is one.

entries.clue: Runs into wood for gun’s component (6)

indicatorNotes.into: R goes into the wood's name.

annotation.surface: Someone flees into the woods to fetch part of a gun.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Runs' looks like a verb of flight; it is the R of a cricket scorecard.
annotation.definitionFit: The breech is the rear part of a gun barrel where it is loaded.

entries.clue: This writer’s demonstrating on the right path? (9)

blocks.note: this writer = I; this writer's = I'M

annotation.surface: The setter claims to be showing they are on the right track.
annotation.walkthrough: 'This writer' is the setter, so I; with the 's read as 'is' it becomes I'M.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone improving is getting better, heading the right way.

entries.clue: Bats eating tip of native plant (7)

indicatorNotes.Bats: Bats means crazy, so the letters go haywire.
indicatorNotes.tip of: The tip of a word is its first letter.

annotation.surface: Bats feeding on the flower of a local plant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Eating' looks like a container instruction around N; it is fodder, rearranged along with N.
annotation.definitionFit: The gentian is a mountain plant with deep blue flowers.

entries.clue: Stealing unusual rug in store (10)

indicatorNotes.unusual: Unusual: the letters are put in an unusual order.

annotation.surface: A shoplifter pockets an odd rug on display in a shop.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In store' looks like a container; the whole phrase RUG IN STORE is the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Trousering money is British slang for pocketing it, often dishonestly.

entries.clue: Permitted female to leave uncultivated expert (9)

indicatorNotes.to leave: F, for female, leaves the word.

annotation.surface: A woman is allowed to walk away from a field lying fallow.
annotation.walkthrough: Fallow land is ploughed but left unsown, so 'uncultivated' gives FALLOW.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: what is allowable is what the rules let through.

entries.clue: Face to show entertaining people (5)

blocks.note: pan = face (slang for the face; also to swing a camera round)

annotation.surface: An instruction to turn and play to the crowd.
annotation.walkthrough: A panto (pantomime) is a British Christmas stage show for families, full of slapstick and audience participation.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: pantomime is the family stage show put on to amuse audiences at Christmas.

entries.clue: In successful campaigns, American guided speeches? (13)

indicatorNotes.In: A and LED go in the word for successful campaigns.

annotation.surface: An American steers the rhetoric of winning election campaigns.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a narrow definition: valedictories are farewell speeches, and in America the valedictorian gives one at graduation.
annotation.definitionFit: A valedictory is a speech of farewell.

entries.clue: Finished with good circular alternative to the Tube? (10)

annotation.surface: Someone done with a nice circular route that avoids the London Underground.
annotation.walkthrough: The Tube is the London Underground; the London Overground is a separate rail network that often loops round the city.
annotation.definitionFit: Travelling overground, on the surface, is the alternative to going by Tube.

entries.clue: State delaying appearance of a commercial centre? It’s true (8)

annotation.definitionNote: The definition is a clause; veracity is the noun for the quality of being true.

indicatorNotes.delaying appearance of a: The A shows up later: it moves from the front of the word to the back.

blocks.note: AVER with its A moved to the end

annotation.surface: A shopping centre opening late, and someone insisting that's true.
annotation.walkthrough: 'State' is the verb: to aver is to state firmly. The City is London's financial district.
annotation.definitionFit: Veracity is truthfulness, the quality of what is true.

entries.clue: Cheat’s endless charm: ultimately evil demon, no saint (9)

indicatorNotes.endless: Endless: the last letter is cut off.
indicatorNotes.ultimately: Ultimately points to the last letter.
indicatorNotes.no: No saint: the S for saint is removed.

annotation.surface: A con artist whose charm hides something demonic and far from saintly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Demon' is SATAN, and 'no saint' drops the S that stands for saint.
annotation.definitionFit: A charlatan is a fraud, someone who cheats by false pretence.

entries.clue: Quiet, internal part of Greater London (6)

annotation.surface: A calm spot in the heart of London.
annotation.walkthrough: Pinner is a suburb in north-west London, in the borough of Harrow.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: this suburb is one of the many districts making up Greater London.

entries.clue: What may make Utes calm when roused? (8)

annotation.definition: What may make Utes calm when roused?

indicatorNotes.when roused: Roused means stirred up, so the letters are stirred.

annotation.surface: Asks what would pacify a Native American people once stirred up.
annotation.walkthrough: The Utes are a Native American people of Utah; a calumet is the ceremonial peace pipe, so the whole clue defines while its middle is the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Calumets, peace pipes, were smoked to make peace.

entries.clue: Call on artist outwardly beaming? (6)

indicatorNotes.on: In an across clue, DIAL placed on RA sits after it.

blocks.note: to dial = to call on the phone

annotation.surface: Phoning a painter who seems to be smiling on the outside.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Beaming' suggests a smile; here it means sending out beams, like spokes from a hub.
annotation.definitionFit: Radial means spreading outward from a centre, like rays.

entries.clue: Gather information following action by reporter about lawyer (7)

indicatorNotes.about: About means turned round, so ED is reversed.

annotation.surface: A journalist gathers facts from a lawyer after some legal action.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About lawyer' wants to be a container round the lawyer; 'about' only turns ED round. A brief is British slang for a barrister.
annotation.definitionFit: To debrief is to question someone after a mission to gather what they learned.

entries.clue: Turn handle and snatch a pole he has? (8)

annotation.definitionNote: The definition is a description: he who has a pole.

indicatorNotes.Turn: Turn means turn round, so NAME GRAB is written backwards.

annotation.surface: Someone twists a handle and grabs a pole.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Handle' looks like a door handle; it is slang for a name. A bargeman punts or steers with a pole.
annotation.definitionFit: A bargeman works a barge and may push it along with a pole.

entries.clue: Gossip — the very thing to support one information unit (7)

indicatorNotes.to support: In a down clue, a supporting piece goes underneath, so GAB IT comes after ME.

annotation.surface: Gossip is just the thing to prop up one's store of information.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One' is ME, and in a down clue 'support' places GAB IT beneath it.
annotation.definitionFit: A megabit is a million bits of data.

entries.clue: Professional model in good health (6)

blocks.note: to sit for an artist is to model

annotation.surface: A professional model who is in fine health.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Good health' is the toast, not a condition. Prosit is the German drinking toast.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: the German toast is said while raising a glass, wishing the drinkers good health.

entries.clue: Seditious labourers being out of line finally sacked (6-7)

indicatorNotes.out: Out means disordered, so the letters rearrange.
indicatorNotes.finally: Finally points to the last letter.
indicatorNotes.sacked: Sacked: the letter is dismissed from the fodder.

blocks.note: last letter of line, removed from the fodder

annotation.surface: Workers step out of line in protest and are fired.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Out of line' reads as a phrase; split it: 'out' is the anagram signal, and 'of line finally sacked' takes an E away.
annotation.definitionFit: Rabble-rousing is stirring up a crowd against authority.

entries.clue: Use of mocking language is smooth? Yes, primarily (5)

annotation.surface: Asks whether sarcasm is a smooth trick, and answers yes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Smooth' reads as an adjective about the mockery; it is the verb, to iron.
annotation.definitionFit: Irony is saying the opposite of what one means, often to mock.

entries.clue: Armed struggle crosses Eastern river (4)

indicatorNotes.crosses: The fight crosses over E, lying on either side of it.

annotation.surface: A war spills over onto the banks of an eastern river.
annotation.walkthrough: The Wear is a river in north-east England, flowing through Durham and Sunderland.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: this is one of the rivers of north-east England.

entries.clue: Type of Christian fighting group capturing area (5)

indicatorNotes.capturing: The group captures A, holding it inside.

annotation.surface: A Christian militia seizing territory.
annotation.walkthrough: A Uniat belongs to an Eastern church that keeps its own rites but accepts the Pope's authority.
annotation.definitionFit: Uniat names a member of an Eastern Catholic church in union with Rome.

entries.clue: Get large drink and suffer the consequences of it? (3,6)

annotation.surface: Order a big drink and pay the price.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Get' pretends to mean fetch a drink; it means understand. The 'it' is the large drink, whose consequence is blurred vision.
annotation.definitionFit: Seeing double is what too much drink does to you.

entries.clue: Half dead court limiting enjoyment is no longer valid (7)

indicatorNotes.Half: 'Half' takes one of the word's two halves, here the first two letters of 'dead'.
indicatorNotes.limiting: The court limits FUN, holding it inside.

annotation.surface: A half-dead court that stifles pleasure has lost its authority.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dead' sits beside 'no longer valid' and tempts as part of the definition; only its first half is used.
annotation.definitionFit: Something defunct has ceased to exist or operate.

entries.clue: Unscrupulous person reticent and mostly severe (7)

indicatorNotes.mostly: Mostly: all but the last letter.

annotation.surface: A crook who is quiet and rather stern.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition paints a rogue, while the wordplay describes someone shy and stern.
annotation.definitionFit: A shyster is a dishonest person, especially a lawyer.
